explanation: Removing shoes when entering someone's home isn't a strict guest custom in Spain the way it is in Japan or Korea — most Spanish homes have tile or hardwood floors, and families typically switch into slippers at home for comfort rather than out of a rule for visitors. As a guest, you're not expected to take your shoes off unless your host does, or asks you to.
local_tip: Watch what your host does — if they're in slippers and offer you a pair, take the hint; otherwise it's fine to keep your shoes on.

also_check.note: Removing shoes before stepping past the genkan (entryway) is mandatory and deeply ingrained.
Norms vary by household; some families expect shoes off, others don't mind, so it's best to follow the host's lead.
As in Japan, removing shoes before entering a home is a firmly established, non-negotiable custom.

sources.title: Why Some Countries Take Off Their Shoes Indoors
